title: hotfix: fix ordering race in SLO enforcer regional fallback (backoff/hysteresis)
author: Aisha Carter
description: Summary: Fix an ordering race in the SLO Enforcer that could cause premature regional failover and excessive load-shedding under bursty traffic. Root cause: when the enforcer path selector applied backoff timers and hysteresis we occasionally observed non-deterministic ordering between the backoff expiration handler and the regional-fallback decision path; this could let a node be considered healthy while its in-flight queues were stale, triggering a failover cascade. This hotfix serializes the decision path, adds a lightweight lock around state transitions, and tightens the ordering of hysteresis and backoff evaluation. Changes include: 1) add a per-region state mutex and ensure failover decision reads happen after backoff/hysteresis evaluation completes, 2) move backoff expiry processing onto the main event loop to preserve ordering guarantees, 3) add metric tags to trace backoff->failover transitions, 4) add unit + integration tests that reproduce the race and assert stable ordering under synthetic bursts, 5) minor telemetry/alert adjustments so SRE can detect related regressions earlier. Why this change: we saw two incidents in the last 30 days (INC-2025-11-03, INC-2025-11-09) where SLO Enforcer oscillated regional routing causing increased tail latency and customer errors. This patch is a targeted hotfix to regain stability while we plan a longer-term refactor to the enforcer execution model. Testing: local unit tests, Kubernetes integration test that replays the incident traffic pattern (added to perf-canary pipeline), and a staged rollout to canary region us-west-2 for 24h. Rollback plan: revert the single commit that introduces the lock and restart the enforcer pods; the change is additive and safe to roll back if any regression observed. Checklist: [x] unit tests added, [x] integration test added to perf-canary, [x] SLO impact reviewed with SRE, [x] metrics/alerts adjusted, [x] staged canary rollout scheduled. Related: Linear ENG-3214, ENG-3301; Jira SUP-4532.

review_comments: Ben Klein (2025-11-12): Request changes - the mutex is coarse-grained; can we ensure it won't become a throughput bottleneck in high QPS regions? Please add a benchmark or explain contention bounds.

Aisha Carter (2025-11-12): Reply - good point. The lock is intentionally per-region and only held for microseconds around state transitions; I added a microbenchmark in ordering_test.go showing <0.2% tail latency impact at 10k RPS and documented the expectation in code comments.

Lina Zhou (2025-11-13): Suggestion - prefer event-loop approach for backoff expiry to preserve ordering (you already adopted this in commit 4c2d1e8). Please add a comment explaining ordering guarantees.
Marco Ruiz (2025-11-13): Approve - verified integration test reproduces the race locally; metrics look good and staged canary in us-west-2 has stable routing for 12h. Approving to merge with squash.
SRE-bot (2025-11-13): Automated run - canary smoke passed; no increased 5xx or queue growth observed in the canary slice.
release_notes: Hotfix: fix race in SLO Enforcer decision ordering causing regional failover oscillations; adds ordering serialization, moves backoff expiry to main event loop, and adds tests and telemetry. Recommended: monitor slo_enforcer.backoff_transition and slo_enforcer.failover_count for 24h post deploy.
notes_for_qa: Run perf-canary pipeline scenario 'slo-enforcer-regional-race' in a cluster with synthetic burst traffic and assert no failover cascades for 10x baseline burst for 5m windows. Verify metrics tags backoff_region and failover_region are present in exported metrics.
why_urgent: This patch addresses recent production incidents where regional routing oscillation caused increased customer-facing errors and tail latency; the fix is targeted and low-risk, and SRE requested expedited rollout.
backout_instructions: kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-enforcer -n redwood; if immediate rollback required, revert commit 7a3f9b2 and restart pods. Monitor slo_enforcer.failover_count and endpoint 5xxs.
